findings.title: Dayjs equality uses === so full-day unavailable override never matches
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable the code tests `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect an unavailable-day override where start equals end. Dayjs instances are objects, so === compares identity and is always false. The branch never fires, dateOverrideExist stays true, and the function later returns true, so a day the host marked as fully unavailable becomes bookable.

findings.title: Slots on date-override days return available without checking busy times
findings.body: After detecting that a slot falls on a date-override day, checkIfIsAvailable does `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` before the busy-calendar check. That early return skips the `busy.every(...)` verification, so existing Cal bookings and external calendar blocks on override days are ignored and double-booking becomes possible.

findings.title: Working-hours end uses start time so events overrunning closing time pass
findings.body: In the working-hours fallback both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute()`. The end should be derived from slot end time (start + eventLength). As written an event that starts inside working hours but ends outside is still considered available, allowing bookings past closing time.

findings.title: Outside-working-hours test uses find so split shifts reject valid slots
findings.body: The code uses `workingHours.find` to look for any entry where the slot is outside that entry and then rejects the slot. With multiple intervals on the same weekday (e.g. morning and afternoon), a slot that fits the second interval still matches the outside condition of the first interval, so find succeeds and the valid slot is incorrectly rejected.

findings.title: Override offset parses via toString and crashes when timeZone missing
findings.body: The override conversion does `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)`. TimeRange.timeZone is optional and can be undefined, in which case tz() is invalid, and toString() round-trips through server locale strings losing millisecond/offset fidelity. This yields NaN or wrong utcOffset, shifting override start/end minutes and producing wrong slots or a runtime error.

findings.title: Active overrides filtered only by start instant misses overlapping day
findings.body: activeOverrides keeps an override only if `dayjs.utc(override.start)` falls inside the invitee day. An override that overlaps the day but starts on an adjacent day due to timezone shift or an evening interval spanning midnight is dropped, so the day falls back to regular working hours and shows wrong availability. The later hour/minute math also drops day overflow, assigning shifted times to the wrong day.

findings.title: No test for round-robin fixed-host override or unavailable/busy override cases
findings.body: The PR claims to fix fixed-host date overrides for round-robin events, but the only added test checks that a personal-event override returns the same UTC slots in two invitee timezones. There is no coverage for fixed vs loose hosts, for start==end unavailable days, or for busy bookings on override days, so the === bug and the early-return that skips busy checks are not caught.
